title: Frontend senior systemdesign cross team design system
topic: Frontend senior systemdesign cross team design system
question: Design a design system meant to be adopted across many product teams at a large company, each with different products, frameworks in some cases, and release cadences. What does this look like end to end?
idealAnswer:
Separate the design system into layers: design tokens (raw values, framework-agnostic), a styling layer, and framework-specific component implementations, so teams on different stacks can still consume shared tokens even without shared components

Provide clear adoption paths for teams that can't do a full migration at once, e.g. token-only adoption, CSS-only adoption, or full component adoption, meeting teams where they are rather than requiring an all-or-nothing switch

Establish a governance model with clear ownership, a contribution process, and a versioning/deprecation policy, since dozens of teams will need to request changes and can't all be blocked on one central team indefinitely

Invest in tooling that makes the system easy to consume correctly, linting rules that catch use of raw hex colors instead of tokens, codemods for migrating from ad hoc styles, and strong documentation with real usage examples

Build in visual regression testing and cross-browser/cross-framework verification as part of the system's own release process, since a bug in a shared button now affects every product, the blast radius of a mistake is much larger than in a single product's codebase

Measure and report adoption (percentage of surfaces using system components/tokens vs legacy styles) to make the migration's progress visible and to justify continued investment to leadership
